    10	/-!
    11	# An inhabited finite-stage Picard glue package
    12	
    13	The simultaneous pair- and triple-transition descent theorems supply every input of
    14	`pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData`.  This file records those dependent inputs in one
    15	package and immediately exposes the resulting scheme glue datum.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
    23	open scoped TensorProduct
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
    34	-- The fields retain three nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
    35	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    36	/-- All finite-stage models and comparison equations needed to assemble the descended
    37	Picard atlas.  The fields are outputs of the simultaneous finite-subextension producers,
    38	not additional geometric hypotheses. -/
    39	structure Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    40	    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] where
    41	  L : DatG0.FinSubext F k
    42	  n : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
    43	  m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
    44	  relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1
    45	  e : forall j,
    46	    k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
    47	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C j
    48	  M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k
    49	  mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
    50	    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    51	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
    52	      Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    53	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)
    54	  hmapM : forall q,
    55	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    56	        (AlgHom.id L.1
    57	          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    58	            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    59	            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    60	            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
    61	        ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
    62	      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
    63	        L.1).comp
    64	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    65	          (AlgHom.id L.1
    66	            (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    67	              (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    68	              (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    69	              (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))
    70	  hOpen : forall i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
    71	    IsOpenImmersion
    72	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))
    73	  N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k
    74	  thetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    75	    N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
    76	        C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
    77	      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
    78	        C L n m relation M mapM p
    79	  hthetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    80	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
    81	        (AlgHom.id M.1
    82	          (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
    83	            C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
    84	        ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
    85	      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
    86	        C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
    87	          M.1).comp
    88	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
    89	          (AlgHom.id M.1
    90	            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
    91	              C L n m relation M mapM p)))
    92	
    93	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

    95	set_option maxHeartbeats 25600000 in
    96	-- The package projections retain the dependent tensor-product instances of the constructor.
    97	/-- The scheme glue datum computed from an inhabited finite-stage package. -/

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChange
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Basic geometry of the finite-stage Picard glue
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue is covered by finitely many affine spectra of explicit
    12	finite-presentation algebras over its field of definition.  Consequently its structure
    13	morphism is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, without any additional geometric
    14	hypothesis on the package.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	variable {k F : Type u} [Field k] [Field F]
    28	variable [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    29	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    34	
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- The chart rings retain two nested finite-subextension tensor products.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure morphism of the finite-stage Picard glue is locally of finite type. -/
    39	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedMap
    40	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    41	    LocallyOfFiniteType P.gluedMap := by
    42	  apply IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover P.glueData.openCover
    43	  intro U
    44	  change LocallyOfFiniteType (P.glueData.ι U ≫ P.gluedMap)

    25	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along open immersions. -/
    26	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    27	    [IsOpenImmersion f] (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    28	  classical
    29	  intro s hs
    30	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := hY (f.base '' s) (hs.image f.base)
    31	  letI : Fintype s := hs.fintype
    32	  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrle⟩ :=
    33	    AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
    34	      (fun x : s => f.base x)
    35	      (fun x => hU ⟨x, x.2, rfl⟩)
    36	      (fun x => Scheme.Hom.mem_opensRange.mpr ⟨(x : X), rfl⟩)
    37	  refine ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ Y.basicOpen r,
    38	    (U.2.basicOpen r).preimage_of_isOpenImmersion f hrle⟩, ?_⟩
    39	  intro x hx
    40	  change f.base x ∈ Y.basicOpen r
    41	  exact hr ⟨x, hx⟩

    44	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    45	    [IsImmersion f] (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    46	  obtain ⟨Z, g₁, g₂, hg₁, hg₂, -⟩ :=
    47	    (AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion.isImmersion_iff_exists (f := f)).mp

1	/-

     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeQProj
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The concrete project-local model of the admissible divisor representer
    11	
    12	The admissible coverage parameter is strictly positive, so the chosen representer in
    13	`DivRepAffChallenge` is definitionally the nonzero `DivScheme` branch.  This file names that
    14	concrete branch and transports its closed immersion into the Grassmannian pair back to
    15	`divRepAffAdmissibleScheme`.
    16	
    17	The resulting certificate is unconditional and geometric: the target has its finite affine
    18	product atlas, and the source is quasi-compact, locally of finite type, and separated over the
    19	base field.  It is not yet a finite-projective-space immersion.  That stronger conclusion needs
    20	the Plucker embeddings of both Grassmannian factors together with their Segre product; those
    21	maps are not present in the rebuild project.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option quotPrecheck false
    26	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8
    28	set_option maxRecDepth 16000
    29	
    30	universe u
    31	
    32	open CategoryTheory
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	open Grassmannian Scheme
    37	
    38	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    39	  Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    40	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    41	
    42	section Curve
    43	
    44	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    45	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    46	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    47	
    48	noncomputable local instance admissibleDivisorOver :
    49	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    50	
    51	local instance admissibleDivisorSmooth :
    52	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    53	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
    54	
    55	local instance admissibleDivisorIntegral : IsIntegral C.left :=
    56	  isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
    57	
    58	local instance admissibleDivisorLocallyOfFiniteType :
    59	    LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    60	  inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
    61	
    62	local instance admissibleDivisorQuasiCompact :
    63	    QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    64	  inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
    65	
    66	noncomputable local instance admissibleDivisorHModuleFiniteZero :
    67	    Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
    68	  moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
    69	
    70	noncomputable local instance admissibleDivisorHModuleFiniteOne :
    71	    Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
    72	  moduleFinite_hModule_one C
    73	
    74	/-- The chosen finite map is over `Spec k`, in the spelling used by the divisor-window API. -/
    75	theorem divRepAffP1Map_comp_over :

     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AmbientPicNotProper
    10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover
    11	
    12	/-!
    13	# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for
    14	
    15	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
    16	subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
    17	of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
    18	on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
    19	written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
    20	quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
    21	hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
    22	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    23	
    24	This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` from the project's
    25	finite-projective-space notion `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective`; projectivity is
    26	the closed-immersion special case.  The chain is
    27	
    28	  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
    29	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
    30	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` H-quasi-projective over `S`.
    31	
    32	## The two avoidance inputs
    33	
    34	The original deep input is the first step, and it is **absent from mathlib
    35	`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
    36	`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
    37	of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
    38	produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
    39	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
    40	Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
    41	where the grading is consumed.
    42	
    43	For a closed immersion the final transport is cheap: `IsClosedImmersion →
    44	IsAffineHom`, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage` pulls affine opens back.  An open
    45	immersion needs a second prime-avoidance step: after placing the finite image in
    46	an affine open, `GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite` shrinks it to a
    47	basic open lying inside the immersion range.  The standard closed/open
    48	factorization then gives transport along every immersion.
    49	
    50	Thus graded avoidance is the new algebraic result in this file.  Open-immersion
    51	transport is the only additional substantive geometric step; its algebra is
    52	delegated to the already-landed finite prime-avoidance theorem.  The remaining
    53	H-quasi-projective and coproduct declarations are factorization and packaging.
    54	
    55	## What this does and does not buy
    56	
    57	It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
    58	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
    59	nothing in this project produces an H-quasi-projective witness for the relevant

     8	/-!
     9	# Projective and H-quasi-projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	A morphism is **H-quasi-projective** when it factors through a quasi-compact
    16	immersion into such a projective space, following the finite-projective-space
    17	convention of [Stacks, Tag 01VV].  The quasi-compactness is part of the
    18	definition: without it the predicate only records an immersion/relative very
    19	ampleness and need not imply finite type.  This predicate is not asserted to
    20	be equivalent over arbitrary bases to every formulation using relative ample
    21	line bundles.  Both predicates are stable under base change.
    22	
    23	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    24	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    25	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    37	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    38	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    39	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    40	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    41	
    42	/-- A morphism is H-quasi-projective if it admits a quasi-compact immersion into
    43	a finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    44	def Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    45	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    46	    IsImmersion i ∧ QuasiCompact i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    47	
    48	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    49	
    50	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    51	
    52	/-- A projective morphism is H-quasi-projective. -/
    53	theorem isHQuasiProjective (h : pi.IsProjective) : pi.IsHQuasiProjective := by
    54	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    55	  letI : Finite n := hn
    56	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
    57	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, inferInstance, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
    58	
    59	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    60	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  rw [← hcomp]
    65	  infer_instance
    66	
    67	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    68	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    69	  haveI := h.isProper
    70	  inferInstance
    71	
    72	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    73	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    74	  haveI := h.isProper
    75	  inferInstance
    76	
    77	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    78	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    79	  haveI := h.isProper
    80	  inferInstance
    81	
    82	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    83	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    84	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    85	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    86	  letI : Finite n := hn
    87	  haveI := hi
    88	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩

    90	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    91	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    92	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    93	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    94	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    95	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    96	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    97	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])

   102	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h

   104	  haveI := hi
   105	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩

   110	      have hbig : IsPullback

   112	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   113	        rw [h1, hcomp]
   114	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   115	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   116	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   117	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   118	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
   119	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   120

   137	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h

   139	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   140	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc

   155	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] :
   156	    (j ≫ pi).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   157	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   158	  letI : Finite n := hn
   159	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   160	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   161	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
   162	
   163	/-- The comparison from a base-changed source to the corresponding base change
   164	of its ambient projective space. -/
   165	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
   166	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
   167	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
   168	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
   169	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
   170	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
   171	
   172	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   173	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   174	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   175	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   176	  letI : Finite n := hn
   177	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   178	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   179	  have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   180	      pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _

   182	      (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   183	    have hbig : IsPullback
   184	        (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   185	        (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   186	      rw [h1, hcomp]
   187	      exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   188	    exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   189	      (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   190	      (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   191	  exact ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp,
   192	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi,
   193	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hqc, h1⟩
   194	
   195	end Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective

   200	theorem isProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   201	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsProjective :=
   202	  ⟨n, inferInstance, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩
